facts.text: On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women’s Day celebrations in the city of Malatya, during which a group comprising hundreds of police officers formed a cordon around the crowd.

facts.text: The police chief warned the participants that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.

facts.text: The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, who was a spokesperson for the Women’s Democratic Platform, told the police chief that they were exercising their constitutional right and that the applicable legislation required no prior permission.

facts.text: Police officers then dragged a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles, sprayed the crowds with tear gas and hit some of them, including the four applicants.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  Police officers then dragged a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles. In the course of so doing, the police officers sprayed the crowds with tear gas and hit some of them, including the four applicants.

facts.text: The second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, was not arrested or beaten but was sprayed with tear gas along with her eleven-year-old daughter and mother.

anchor.surface_text: 10.  The second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, was not arrested. She was not beaten up, but was sprayed with tear gas. She was accompanied by her eleven-year-old daughter and her mother, both of whom were also sprayed with tear gas.

facts.text: In the police vehicles, male police officers squeezed the arms and legs of the detained women, who asked for female officers and were sworn at; this lasted about twenty minutes.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  The ill-treatment continued in the police vehicles. Male police officers started squeezing the arms and legs of the detained women. When the women told the police officers that they had no right to behave like that and asked for female police officers to accompany them, they were sworn at. The episode in the police vehicles lasted for approximately twenty minutes.

facts.text: The four applicants were taken to a police station and then to the Forensic Medicine Institute for medical examination, with reports noting injuries preventing work for one to three days.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  The four applicants were then taken to a police station and subsequently to the Forensic Medicine Institute for a medical examination. According to the medical reports drawn up that day, the four applicants who had been hit by the police officers had a number of injuries on their bodies, rendering them unable to work for periods of between one and three days.

facts.text: Later that same day the four applicants were released from police custody.

anchor.surface_text: 13.  Later that same day the four applicants were released from police custody.

facts.text: On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women’s Day Celebrations in Malatya where three different groups of demonstrators were carrying placards, flags and posters, and holding demonstrations which hindered the flow of traffic.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women’s Day Celebrations in Malatya where three different groups of demonstrators were carrying placards, flags and posters, and holding demonstrations which hindered the flow of traffic.

facts.text: A group of police officers tried to convince the group to disperse and requested them to hold their demonstrations without impeding traffic; the police chief warned no prior permission had been obtained but allowed demonstration on the pavement.

anchor.surface_text: 15.  A group of police officers tried to convince the group to disperse, and requested them to hold their demonstrations without impeding the circulation of the traffic. A police chief warned the participants that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering, but told them that they could carry on with their demonstration on the pavement and walk in an orderly manner without violating public order.

facts.text: The group, including the applicants, refused to disperse and continued with their demonstration, shouting slogans and blocking the street despite police warnings.

anchor.surface_text: Nevertheless, the group, including the applicants, refused to disperse and continued with their demonstration. The police chief made several unsuccessful attempts to tell the participants that the manner in which they were conducting their demonstration was unlawful because they were impeding the flow of traffic.

facts.text: Ten to fifteen police officers formed a cordon around the participants who had been giving orders to the rest of the demonstrators.

anchor.surface_text: Meanwhile, ten to fifteen police officers formed a cordon around the participants who had been giving orders to the rest of the demonstrators.

facts.text: Police officers put a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles by force which could not be considered disproportionate and took them to the Malatya Court House.

anchor.surface_text: 18.  Police officers then put a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into the waiting police vehicles by force which could not be considered disproportionate. They were taken to the Malatya Court House.

facts.text: On the way to the court house the applicants insulted the police officers and tried to provoke them, but the police officers kept calm; female demonstrators were accompanied by female police officers.

anchor.surface_text: On the way to the court house the applicants insulted the police officers present in the vehicle and tried to provoke them. However, the police officers kept their calm. Female demonstrators were accompanied by female police officers in the vehicle.

facts.text: The remaining members of the group who had not been arrested continued with their demonstration and read out their press release after complying with police requests.

anchor.surface_text: 19.  The remaining members of the group who had not been arrested continued with their demonstration and read out their press release after having complied with the police officers’ request to fold their placards and walk on the pavement.

facts.text: According to a report signed by eighteen police officers, at 2.00 p.m. on 8 March 2005, police received intelligence that NGOs planned to gather at the junction of Milli Egemenlik Street to march to the square outside the post office.

anchor.surface_text: 22.  According to a report signed by eighteen police officers, at 2.00 p.m. on 8 March 2005, police received intelligence that a number of non-governmental organisations were planning to gather at the junction of Milli Egemenlik Street with a view to marching from there to the square outside the post office.

facts.text: The police put in place all necessary security measures at the junction at 11.00 a.m. and the demonstrators began arriving at midday.

anchor.surface_text: The police put in place all necessary security measures at the junction at 11.00 a.m. and the demonstrators began arriving at midday.

facts.text: The police officers unsuccessfully urged the demonstrators not to march with their placards to the square where a press release was scheduled to be read out.

anchor.surface_text: 23.  The police officers unsuccessfully urged the demonstrators not to march with their placards to the square, where a press release was scheduled to be read out.

facts.text: The police officers had to use force to arrest the applicants (except the second applicant) and five other demonstrators because they resisted arrest and insulted the police officers.

anchor.surface_text: When the demonstrators ignored the police and started marching, thus blocking a main road, the police officers had to use force to arrest the applicants – with the exception of the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir – and five other demonstrators because they resisted arrest and insulted the police officers.

facts.text: The Government submitted video footage of the incident, but the part where police used force and arrested the applicants does not feature in the footage.

anchor.surface_text: 25.  The Government submitted to the Court the video footage of the incidents recorded by police officers. However, the part where the police officers used force and arrested the applicants does not feature in the footage.

facts.text: On 8 March 2005 the second applicant lodged an official complaint with the prosecutor against the police officers who sprayed her and her daughter with tear gas.

anchor.surface_text: 29.  On 8 March 2005 the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, lodged an official complaint with the prosecutor against the police officers who, she alleged, had sprayed her and her daughter with tear gas.

facts.text: On 11 March 2005 the remaining four applicants lodged an official complaint with the prosecutor against the police officers allegedly responsible for ill-treatment, complaining they had been beaten while exercising their rights.

anchor.surface_text: 30.  On 11 March 2005 the remaining four applicants lodged an official complaint with the prosecutor against the police officers allegedly responsible for the ill-treatment. They complained, inter alia, that they had been beaten up and assaulted while exercising their right to freedom of expression and assembly.

facts.text: Between 4 April 2005 and 3 May 2005 the Malatya prosecutor took statements from eighteen police officers who had been on duty on the day of the incidents.

anchor.surface_text: 32.  Between 4 April 2005 and 3 May 2005 the Malatya prosecutor took statements from eighteen police officers who had been on duty on the day of the incidents.

facts.text: On 12 May 2005 the Malatya prosecutor decided not to prosecute the police officers, stating the applicants had gathered without prior permission and had resisted arrest and insulted police.

anchor.surface_text: 36.  On 12 May 2005 the Malatya prosecutor decided not to prosecute the police officers. In his decision the prosecutor stated that the second applicant, Ms İspir, had been unable to recognise the police officer who had sprayed her with tear gas. The prosecutor stated that the applicants had gathered in the area without having sought prior permission. In dispersing the unauthorised demonstration, the police officers had been impelled to resort to the use of force in order to apprehend the applicants because they had resisted arrest and insulted them.

facts.text: The applicants lodged an objection against the prosecutor’s decision, arguing they had not resisted arrest and had tried to exercise their right to freedom of expression.

anchor.surface_text: 37.  The applicants lodged an objection against the prosecutor’s decision. They argued, in particular, that although they had not resisted arrest, the police officers had proceeded to arrest them by using force. The applicants also maintained that they had tried to exercise their right to freedom of expression, which was guaranteed by the Constitution as well as by Article 10 of the Convention.

facts.text: The objection filed by the applicants was rejected by the Elazığ Assize Court on 28 July 2005.

anchor.surface_text: 38.  The objection filed by the applicants was rejected by the Elazığ Assize Court on 28 July 2005.

facts.text: On 8 March 2005 four of the applicants were questioned by the Malatya prosecutor as suspects and denied insulting police officers, stating they were arrested without warning and hit.

anchor.surface_text: 39.  On 8 March 2005 four of the applicants – that is, all the applicants with the exception of the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir – were questioned by the Malatya prosecutor as suspects. They told the prosecutor that before they could even begin their demonstration the police had arrested them without warning and, in the course of doing so, had hit them. They denied that they had insulted the police officers.

facts.text: On 8 March 2005 the Malatya prosecutor filed an indictment and brought criminal proceedings against the four applicants and five others for insulting police officers and contravening the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act.

anchor.surface_text: 40.  On the same day, the Malatya prosecutor filed an indictment with the Malatya Criminal Court of First Instance and brought criminal proceedings against the four applicants, as well as against the remaining five persons who had been arrested together with the applicants, for insulting the police officers and contravening the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).

facts.text: On 2 June 2005 the Malatya Criminal Court of First Instance acquitted the four applicants and the remaining defendants, holding no evidence showed resistance against police officers.

anchor.surface_text: 41.  On 2 June 2005 the Malatya Criminal Court of First Instance acquitted the four applicants and the remaining defendants. It held that there was no evidence to show that the four applicants had put up resistance against the police officers.
